content:
olivia: Hey team — first week PR question. I opened my very first PR against `main` (tiny doc fix + lint) and it got a few style comments. Quick question: do we prefer feature branches (feat/<ticket>) or short-lived topic branches (olivia/xxxx)?

maya: Welcome! We generally prefer feature branches named like `feat/<ticket-number>-short-desc` for anything user-facing or larger. For tiny docs/typos it's ok to use `fix/docs-olivia` or `olivia/<short>` if you include the issue or PR description.

olivia: Thanks — the reviewers suggested splitting a small helper into a utils module. Is there a style guide for folder structure for helpers?

rafa: For runtime helpers we prefer `pkg/<area>/utils` only if reused across packages. Otherwise keep helper private to the package (named `helpers.py` or `_helpers.go`) to avoid surface area. See the contrib guide pattern in the repo root (`CONTRIBUTING.md` section: Packaging & helpers).

olivia: I couldn't find that section quickly. Is there a direct link?

maya: Try this link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#packaging-and-helpers — if that 404s ping me.

olivia: Got it, thanks. Another small thing: CI failed on a lint rule about max-line-length 100 — do we wrap long comments or bump the setting?

derek: We enforce 100 in python and 120 in go by default. For exceptions: 1) long URLs in tests 2) generated files. For comments, wrap if reasonable. If wrapping harms readability (e.g., YAML examples) add `# noqa: E501` with a short justification.

rafa: Also you can run `make fmt` and `make lint` locally — faster than pushing.

olivia: Thanks — ran `make lint` and fixed one remaining flake. Opened a follow-up commit.

maya: Nice. One reviewer nit: please add a short PR description template line linking to the ticket and a short rationale for the helper move. Helps reviewers.

olivia: Will do. Last: branching strategy question — do we rebase or merge when bringing `main` into feature?

derek: We prefer a clean history, so rebase your branch onto `main` before merge if there are conflicts. For big merges we sometimes do a squash merge on the repo-side and keep the PR history tidy — check the repo's merge settings in the GitHub UI.

olivia: Cool. Anything else I should watch for on first PRs?

maya: Add a short test if you touched logic, add a changelog entry only for user-visible changes, and mark the PR with `team:eng-runtime` if it touches runtime.

olivia: Awesome, thank you all! This was faster than hunting docs. :smile:

devex-bot: Reminder: New contributors, please complete the "First PR checklist" in the PR body — see .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md

rafa: If you want, DM me the PR and I can give a quick pre-review.

olivia: Will do — sending link now. Thanks again!
